title: Chapter 68
content:
The steel flashed in a vicious, blinding arc toward his throat.

Jakyeong gave ground, widening the distance between them step by step. With a calm, deliberate movement, he slipped off his designer sunglasses and set them onto the marble sink counter.

"Who sent you, you little punk?!" Choi Man-sik roared, blood trickling from the raw friction burn around his throat. "Was it President Park?! Or Kim?!"

You certainly haven't run short on mortal enemies either.

When Jakyeong offered only cold silence, the giant lunged with the serrated blade. Jakyeong caught the descending wrist with both hands, twisting the joint violently backward and driving his entire body weight into Man-sik’s chest. The man slammed hard against the tiled wall, the knife slipping from his numb fingers and clattering to the floor.

Jakyeong kicked the blade across the tiles and ducked under a heavy, incoming right hook. As Man-sik’s eyes darted toward the weapon, Jakyeong drove a sharp, rising uppercut straight into his jaw. Bone crunched beneath the impact, snapping the giant's head back and knocking him off-balance.

Man-sik swung again. The strike was sluggish, but the fist was heavy as a boulder—a direct hit would fracture a skull. Jakyeong parried the blow, kicked off the partition wall to gain altitude, and slammed his knee straight into the man's nose.

Cartilage shattered. Jakyeong pivoted on his landing foot, unleashing a blistering spin kick that sent the heavy syndicate boss crashing to the floor.

Man-sik staggered back to his feet, shaking the fog from his head as crimson poured freely from his crushed nostrils.

"You arrogant little rat... I'll rip you apart!"

Snorting like a wounded bull, Man-sik charged blindly. They traded a frantic exchange of close-quarters strikes until a heavy backhand caught Jakyeong across the cheek. The sheer force made the room spin. Damn it.Dragging this out was a losing game against raw mass.

Jakyeong ran his tongue along the inside of his bleeding lip, letting out a thin, wicked smirk.

"You find this funny? I'll make today your death day, you little bastard."

"Your brother said the exact same thing," Jakyeong whispered coldly.

Man-sik’s bloodshot pupils contracted.

"Your nephew, too."

A ferocious, unhinged fury flared behind the giant's eyes.

"You're that son of a bitch!"

Infuriated beyond reason, Man-sik charged headlong. In close-quarters combat, blinding rage was the quickest path to a mistake. Kang Il-hyun was a master of exploiting that truth—nobody in the underworld possessed a greater talent for provoking people into homicidal madness.

Jakyeong slipped inside the wide swing, whipped the severed garrote from his waistband, looped it around Man-sik’s throat, and pivoted behind him. As the giant clawed frantically at his neck, Jakyeong dropped his center of gravity, throwing all his leverage into a flawless shoulder throw that slammed Man-sik flat onto his back.

Before the man could recover, Jakyeong snatched a heavy ceramic vase from the vanity and brought it down across the back of the dazed skull.

The porcelain exploded in a concussive burst of shards. Man-sik collapsed face-down on the tiles, paralyzed by the blunt trauma. Jakyeong mounted the heavy back, planting his knees into the spine to pin the weight, and hauled the cord taut with everything he had left.

The massive frame heaved.

Strangled, wet gasps tore from the crushed windpipe as Man-sik’s palms slapped the floor in a frantic, desperate tap. Jakyeong showed zero mercy, leaning his full weight back on the line. The violent spasms gradually subsided into faint twitches until the giant went completely limp, like soaked laundry left on a line.

A series of heavy knocks rattled the restroom entrance, followed by muffled voices.

Confirming the pulse was entirely gone, Jakyeong dragged the heavy corpse into the far stall. Scooping Man-sik’s discarded knife from the floor, he slid his sunglasses back over his eyes and turned the deadbolt.

The door eased open. Two imposing enforcers stood outside with grim expressions, only to freeze when their eyes caught the fresh crimson splattered across Jakyeong's shirt.

"Excuse me," Jakyeong said calmly, brushing past them.

The distraction bought only seconds. As he descended the VIP staircase, a squad of armed men came stampeding toward the upper restrooms.

On the main floor, the patrons continued dancing under the flashing strobes, entirely oblivious to the execution above. Jakyeong strode toward the security foyer at an unhurried pace.

At the turnstiles, a heavy-set guard pressing a finger to his earpiece looked up with a hardened glare, reaching inside his jacket for his sidearm.

Jakyeong raised both hands to shoulder height, feigning surrender. The surrounding crowd began to murmur in unease. Jakyeong extended an open palm as if showing he was unarmed. In the split second the guard’s gaze dipped toward his fingers, Jakyeong struck—seizing the barrel, wrenching it toward the ceiling, and ejecting the magazine in one seamless sweep.

The hammer dropped on an empty chamber with a hollow click.

Drawing Man-sik’s serrated blade from his back, Jakyeong drove the steel into the guard's throat and flank in two surgical thrusts. As crimson arterial spray painted the wall, the entrance crowd erupted into hysterical shrieks, scattering in pure panic.

Jakyeong stripped the sidearm from the falling body, slapped the magazine home, and racked the slide.

Looking back, the rest of the security detail was pouring down the stairs with weapons drawn. Jakyeong ripped a fire extinguisher from the wall bracket, rolled the heavy canister into the middle of the concourse, and fired two rounds into the pressurized cylinder.

The tank ruptured with concussive force, spewing a blinding cloud of white chemical powder across the floor. He fired a third round into the overhead lighting grid, showering the stairwell in blinding electrical sparks.

Screaming clubgoers stampeded blindly through the whiteout, swallowing the pursuing guards in the crush.

Jakyeong bolted into the underground garage. Spotting him through the gloom, the secondary perimeter guards opened fire.

Rounds chipped into the concrete pillars, raining dust over his head. Weaving low between parked luxury vehicles, Jakyeong tore the rear door of the armored sedan open and dove inside.

The moment the latch engaged, Wang Han checked him over for wounds while Wang Ryun floored the accelerator. The tires shrieked against the sealed concrete, the sedan sweeping around the support pillars and launching up the exit ramp into the city streets.

Automatic fire raked the rear windshield, the reinforced ballistic glass catching the slugs without spiderwebbing.

Bursting into the main thoroughfare, several dark SUVs peeled out from the flanking lanes, locking onto their bumper in aggressive pursuit. Given the dense downtown congestion, a prolonged chase would leave them boxed in.

"That got the blood pumping," Ryun laughed, gripping the wheel tight.

"Stop joking around and drive," Han snapped, bracing an arm against the dash.

Ryun threw the wheel left through a red light, threading the sedan between oncoming traffic. A heavy commercial truck blared its horn as it swept past their rear bumper by bare inches.

Without shedding speed, Ryun hooked the sedan down a narrow alleyway. The chassis pitched violently, prompting Ryun to curse as he fought the steering, while Jakyeong tracked the pursuers through the rear glass.

Two of the SUVs were barreling down the narrow passage behind them.

"Right here! Take the next left!" Han called out, navigating by memory.

Ryun whipped the wheel with practiced precision, carving a frantic path through the labyrinthine neon alleys of the motel district. Drifting around a blind corner, he cut the engine and glided the car beneath the heavy canvas awning of a rundown love motel.

Sitting in dead silence, the three held their breath.

Through the gaps in the canvas, a convoy of black pursuit vehicles sped past on the street outside, tires splashing through the rain.

When the road cleared, the tension evaporated from the cabin. All three let out a long, synchronized exhale, leaning their heads back against the headrests.

Ryun stepped outside to swap their cloned plates. As he did, the burner phone in Jakyeong's pocket chimed.

He answered to hear Park Tae-soo’s flat, professional baritone.

[Are you safe, sir?]

The intelligence network moves fast.

"Yes... We're holding in a private parking structure for now. My apologies—I intended to keep it quiet, but the situation spiraled."

[Our support units are on standby in the district. Stay in position until the cordon thins; I will notify you when the route is clear.]

Tae-soo ended the call without another word.

The trio stepped out of the vehicle, paid cash at the front desk, and took the keys to a top-floor room. The cheap motel was draped in gaudy crimson wallpaper, mirrored ceilings, and a stained velvet sofa.

Jakyeong drew the heavy drapes shut, peering through the slit. An unmarked sedan from Il-hyun's security detail was parked two blocks down, while several hostile vehicles continued to circle the outer perimeter.

As he let the fabric fall, the screen illuminated again.

The contact name read: The Bastard.

Jakyeong paused for a second before accepting the line.

[It's me.]

"I know."

[Are you all right?]

"Not really. You've probably heard by now, but the clean extraction fell apart."

[I'm asking if you're bleeding.]

The quiet, immediate concern in the baritone carried an odd, disarming weight. Jakyeong shifted his eyes toward his brothers. Han was inspecting the fire escape, but Ryun was watching him like a hyena sizing up fresh prey, practically salivating for fresh teasing material.

Jakyeong carried the phone into the bathroom, shutting the door behind him.

"I'm fine. But Man-sik’s crew has locked down the surrounding grid, so we can't move for the next few hours."

[Shall I come collect you?]

Jakyeong scowled. "Why not just put up a billboard announcing my coordinates while you're at it?"

A low, soft chuckle came through the speaker. Il-hyun dropped the subject, but the underlying relief in his breath was unmistakable. Uncomfortable with the intimacy, Jakyeong moved to sever the connection, but Il-hyun spoke first.

[You never answered my question from earlier. What kind of flowers do you prefer?]

Jakyeong searched his memory, recalling the bouquet of dark roses the man had brought during their first meeting a year ago. Knowing little about botanical names and wishing to end the call, he muttered, "Roses."

[I knew it,] Il-hyun murmured with a quiet, velvet laugh.

The call clicked dead.

A moment later, an image file landed in the inbox.

It was a photograph of the nightstand in Jakyeong’s guest suite back at the estate. Sitting in a heavy crystal vase beside the bed was a massive arrangement of freshly trimmed red roses. There was no accompanying caption.

Did the bastard actually arrange those himself?

Staring at the petals on the glowing screen for a long, quiet moment, Jakyeong hit delete and stepped back into the bedroom.

The room was vacant. Hearing shuffling in the corridor, he tucked his sidearm behind his back and opened the door. Han and Ryun were stepping inside, their arms loaded with heavy tactical duffels retrieved from the vehicle.

"Call finished?" Ryun asked.

"Yeah..."

"Those bastards are still combing the main avenue."

"Let's rest here until dawn and move when the shift changes," Han suggested. "Turn on some music to mask our voices."

A brief, silent understanding passed between the three men.

Han cranked the television volume to a blaring pop broadcast while Ryun pried open the motel wardrobe. Resting in the recess were fresh changes of clothes, discreet sneakers, and reinforced travel bags pre-staged by their underground contacts.

Ryun unzipped the tactical trunk from the car—not revealing munitions, but dense, vacuum-sealed bricks of foreign currency.

Methodically, Ryun began transferring the stacks of bills into the travel luggage. Jakyeong knelt beside him on the carpet, taking the remaining bundles and packing them flat along the base.

Not a single word was spoken between the three.

They simply worked in disciplined, absolute silence, packing their escape funds into the dark.
